notes: Panel products need grade/thickness normalization in addition to species.
CDX is a plywood grade/construction term, not a species.
Often abbreviated DF-L or sold as Douglas Fir/Doug Fir; may refer to a formal species combination.
Hem-Fir is a species combination of Western Hemlock and true firs.
MDF is engineered fiberboard; not lumber species.
Maple may mean hard, soft, or mixed maple unless specified.
OSB is an engineered panel; not solid lumber.
Oak is broad; red/white oak should be separated if known.
Retailers may label pine boards broadly as pine/common board; exact pine species may not be explicit.
Poplar may be labeled tulip poplar or yellow poplar; often appearance/project board.
Pressure-treated lumber in many U.S. markets is commonly pine/Southern Pine, but verify local supplier/species.
SPF is a species group; whitewood is a seller/trade term and exact species can vary.
Southern Pine includes multiple pine species; SYP and yellow pine are common commercial terms.
Cedar labels can be broad; Western Red Cedar is commonly abbreviated WRC.
White pine may be sold as pine/common board/appearance board; not the same as whitewood.
